events.text: ADR-003, written in 2016: we chose MySQL 5.6 as the ledger database because the team already operated it and its replication was well understood.
ADR-003 was superseded by ADR-019 in 2021: the ledger moved to PostgreSQL because we needed transactional DDL and native JSON columns.
The ledger database runs PostgreSQL 13.
The ledger database runs PostgreSQL 15 after the March 2024 upgrade.
The ledger database runs PostgreSQL 16 after the January 2026 upgrade.
Payment events are published to the Kafka topic ledger-events, which has 12 partitions.
In 2019 we picked Kafka over RabbitMQ because auditors require us to replay a full week of payment events.
The payments on-call rotation is owned by the Platform team.
Since April 2025 the payments on-call rotation is owned by the Ledger Reliability team.
The public payments API allows 600 requests per minute per merchant.
Someone in chat guessed the payments API limit might be 1000 requests per minute; nobody confirmed it.
Card authorization calls time out after 8 seconds.
Card authorization calls now time out after 5 seconds to stay inside the processor SLA.
Deploys to the payments cluster are frozen for the Black Friday window.
Production deploys for payments happen on Tuesdays and Thursdays.
The staging Stripe API key is sk_test_51HalcyonStagingKey.
Incident INC-2207 in 2023: a schema migration locked the ledger table for 40 minutes, so ledger migrations must now be online and batched.
Ledger schema changes run through the online migration tool and need a DBA reviewer before merge.
The mobile app API allows 120 requests per minute per device.
The mobile app on-call rotation is owned by the Apps team.
The ledger database runs Oracle 19c.
The Ledger Room on the third floor is booked for the quarterly finance review.
Book club is reading Kafka's The Trial; we meet on Friday.
The ledger stores amounts as integer minor units together with an ISO 4217 currency code.
Exchange rates are fetched hourly from the ECB feed and cached for 60 minutes.
We cache exchange rates for an hour because the ECB publishes once per business day and rate-limit errors from the feed broke checkout in 2022.
The payments service is deployed only in eu-west-1.
Since the 2024 expansion the payments service runs in eu-west-1 and us-east-1.
A draft proposal suggested adding ap-southeast-2 for payments, but it was never approved.
We never store card numbers; only processor tokens are kept so we stay in PCI SAQ-A scope.
Failed webhook deliveries are retried with exponential backoff for up to 24 hours.
